spec.title: PROP-074 — User project and per-project overrides: user-scoped packages, late boot lanes and user memory
spec.p: Framework record, owner request 2026-11-08. Status `spec/plan`: the shape below is decided, the details are settled during implementation, which follows the cache-stable SYSTEM prefix work (campaign node `USER-PROJECT`, after `SYS-PROMPT`). Nothing here is implemented yet.

p.USER-PROJECT-PURPOSE: A user installs specification packages (flows, skills, stacks and the like) for themselves, not for one repository, with `vibe install -g`. Those packages form a separate tree in a per-user project. Every agent session in any vibevm project also loads that tree last, so it works as an advanced, structured, versioned `MEMORY.md` that follows the user across projects and machines.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT: One per-user project under the vibe settings root, a full ordinary vibevm project: its own `vibe.toml`, lock, `vibevm/vibedeps/`, and an authored `vibevm/vibespecs/` tree (PROP/FEAT documents, boot sources, a user boot snippet). It is compiled, checked and updated by the same machinery as any project; no second compiler or loader exists.

p.USER-PROJECT-REUSE: The existing service user project that `vibe install -g mcp:…` materialises (PROP-027 REG-USER-PROJECT-MATERIALISATION) is the precedent. The specification project and the MCP service project remain separate under USER-PROJECT-ROOT-PATH and USER-PROJECT-ROOT-DECISION. A service scope is carried explicitly by the CLI, never inferred from a path.

p.USER-PROJECT-INSTALL: `vibe install -g` of a specification package targets the user project; application and MCP packages keep their current `-g` meaning. `vibe update -g`, `vibe uninstall -g`, `vibe list -g` and `vibe check -g` operate on it with the ordinary project laws (locked sources, rollback, cooperative stop).

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-PATH: The personal specification project lives at `<settings>/user-project`, where `<settings>` is resolved by the existing settings-root authority, including `VIBE_SETTINGS`. This is separate from the existing `<settings>/mcp/user-project` service project. No command migrates, merges or resets the MCP project implicitly. Runtime adapters resolve settings and pass the resulting root explicitly to ordinary project operations; a pure root calculation performs no filesystem or environment access.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT: `vibe user init` explicitly initializes the personal specification project without requiring a repository in the current directory. The initial manifest is an ordinary `[project]` manifest with `name = "vibe-user"` and `version = "1.0.0"`. It is not a package identity, service registration or globally unique user identifier. Authored records use the ordinary `vibevm/vibespecs/` layout. Initialization does not select a launcher, change harness settings, initialize Git, install packages, contact a registry, or create a SYSTEM template. Lockfiles and compiled boot outputs are produced only by their existing ordinary owners when needed, never fabricated by initialization.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT-SAFETY: An absent root or an existing empty directory may be initialized. An existing valid ordinary project is preserved and reported as already initialized, without rewriting authored bytes or modification times. A nonempty directory without a valid project manifest, a malformed or unsupported manifest, a non-directory root, or a symbolic-link/reparse alias at the destination or an existing ancestor is an explicit refusal; initialization does not adopt, repair or overwrite it. Concurrent initializers must not overwrite each other's manifest. On failure or cancellation, preserve pre-existing user data and remove only operation-owned artifacts when their ownership is proven; otherwise report the incomplete state rather than deleting it speculatively.

p.USER-PROJECT-STATUS: `vibe user status` reports the resolved personal root and whether it is absent, initialized or unavailable, with the reason and explicit initialization or repair surface. An absent project is a normal status, not implicit permission to create it. An unavailable settings root or invalid existing project is reported as unavailable with a nonzero exit. Status performs no writes, installation, compilation, network access or harness launch. Boot and other read-only discovery paths likewise never initialize the project merely because it is absent.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-DECISION: Decision, 2026-11-15: keep the specification project separate and initialize it explicitly through ordinary project machinery. Why: the current MCP project owns service registrations and its own pinned dependency lifecycle; combining the roots would make personal specification operations alter service state without an explicit service scope. Rejected: silently reusing or migrating the MCP root, creating the personal project at every boot, and implementing a second manifest/lock/compiler stack. Revisit only when an owner-approved unified service/specification lifecycle defines registration, locking and migration semantics and its compatibility tests cover existing MCP installations. The root and initialization choices settle only this portion of USER-PROJECT-OPEN; routing, discovery, composition and override decisions remain separate work.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-ADMISSION: For these personal-root operations the selected settings path must be absolute. A relative value is reported as unavailable with a remedy naming an absolute `VIBE_SETTINGS`; it is not silently resolved against the invocation directory. This admission rule does not change the existing settings resolver or other commands' treatment of relative overrides. Reason: an ordinary change of working directory must not select another personal project. Revisit only with an explicit stable base for relative personal-root bindings; implicit cwd resolution is rejected.

p.USER-PROJECT-INITIALIZED-CRITERION: Initialized means that a bounded, stable, no-follow read of the root `vibe.toml` passes the ordinary in-memory manifest parser and semantic validation and contains `[project]`. A project that also declares `[workspace]` is admitted; a package-only or virtual-workspace-only manifest is not. This observation does not traverse workspace members, validate neighboring SYSTEM inputs, inspect lock integrity or establish boot freshness. Status identifies this limited scope rather than claiming the whole project is healthy. Existing projects need no authored directory to qualify, and init never fills missing directories in an already initialized project.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT-PUBLICATION: For a newly initialized project, the persistent output set is `vibe.toml` plus empty `vibevm/` and `vibevm/vibespecs/` directories, along with any missing ancestors of the selected root. No other authored files, boot directory, lockfile or ignore file is created. Prepare the authored directories before publishing the manifest with no-replace semantics; the manifest is the initialization visibility boundary. Temporary operation-owned staging is allowed but is never mistaken for an initialized project. Do not create a project lock or other file before classifying an existing directory as admissible. Status on an absent root or an empty root without a manifest reports absent; nonempty residue without an admitted manifest reports unavailable.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT-RACES: Concurrent init permits one creator and another observer returning already initialized after independently admitting the published manifest. A contender that observes pre-publication nonempty state or input movement may instead refuse with an explicit concurrent-or-incomplete-state diagnostic and retry guidance; success for every contender is not promised. Never interpret arbitrary residue as proof of another initializer's ownership. Failure before manifest publication may leave explicitly reported incomplete directories when safe cleanup cannot be proved. Cancellation after successful publication reports that initialization was committed rather than rolling back a project another process may already use. No command automatically repairs or deletes ambiguous residue.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-REPORT: Init and status share one typed observation, protocol `vibe-user-project/1`, registered as `cli-user-project-report` with authoritative schema `schemas/user_project_report.jtd.json`. Required fields are `protocol`, `ok` (boolean), `command` (`user:init` or `user:status`), `root` (nullable string), `state` (`absent`, `initialized`, `unavailable`), `outcome` (`created`, `already-initialized`, `observed`, `refused`, `incomplete`), `effects` (`none`, `changed`, `unknown`), `publication` (`not-started`, `restored`, `committed`, `recovery-required`), and nullable `reason` and `remedy` strings. Root is the admitted absolute path in the existing machine-path encoding, even if it does not exist; missing or relative settings yield null, never an empty string or cwd guess. No manifest content, credential, timestamp or user identity is included. Existing optional CLI context stamps remain transport metadata.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-REPORT-EFFECTS: Effects describe only this invocation, not old residue or another initializer: `none` means no surviving owned mutation is established and none is uncertain; `changed` means surviving owned changes are established; `unknown` means their survival cannot be determined. Publication refers to this invocation's initialization transaction, not merely to the existence of a manifest: `not-started` means no mutating initialization began, `restored` means its effects were proven undone, `committed` means manifest publication succeeded, and `recovery-required` means mutation began but neither completion nor full restoration is established. Created maps to initialized/created/changed/committed with ok=true. Reinit maps to initialized/already-initialized/none/not-started with ok=true. Status maps to observed/none/not-started, with ok=true for absent or initialized and false for unavailable. A refusal before writes maps to unavailable/refused/none/not-started. A failed mutating init maps to unavailable/incomplete with ok=false, effects and publication reported from actual evidence. Pre-existing incomplete residue alone never implies changed or recovery-required for a read-only observer. An unknown write outcome is not encoded as changed=true.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-REPORT-TRANSPORT: In JSON mode successful operations emit one root report on stdout through the existing CLI context renderer. Typed root-operation failures attach the same observation as the optional `user_project` member of the existing generic stderr error envelope, preserving its error chain and exit status; they do not first emit a root report on stdout. Errors before operation dispatch retain their existing envelope without a promised root observation. Acknowledged cancellation uses only the existing `vibe-project-cancellation/1` terminal envelope and exit 130, with the operation's publication state propagated accurately; it does not emit a second root terminal report. Existing progress events are not additional terminal reports. Plain and quiet output retain state, root when known, and actionable reason/remedy without pretending the observation is whole-project validation. The global JSON/context and cancellation contracts are not replaced by this feature.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-GRAMMAR: The initial grammar is `vibe user init` and `vibe user status`, with existing global output and cancellation options inherited. Neither verb accepts a positional root, `--path`, `-g`, `--force` or a second root override; the existing settings authority is the sole selector. Later operations are not shipped as placeholder commands. Status is a read-only metadata operation; initialization uses the existing finite-operation progress convention.

p.USER-LANE-SEPARATE: The user project produces its own boot lane from its own compilation. A repository's boot lane never embeds or copies it, so a teammate who clones the repository gets the identical project boot and no trace of another person's user lane.

p.USER-LANE-LAST: The user lane is always loaded dynamically, after the static lane, after every entry of the project's boot index and after any live continuation the SYSTEM work defines; only the project override lane (§5), when present, loads after it. A project may not reorder either earlier.

p.USER-LANE-OUTSIDE-PREFIX: The user lane never participates in the project's cache-stable SYSTEM prefix (`SYSTEM-PROMPT-SPEC`): changing or installing a user package never changes the project prefix bytes or invalidates its cache. It may enter only the separate, git-ignored composed prefix of LAYERED-PREFIX.

p.USER-LANE-ABSENT-OK: A missing, empty or broken user project never blocks a project session: the session boots as without it and diagnostics say what was skipped and why.

p.USER-LANE-PRECEDENCE: Loaded last does not mean ranked highest. Project rules (commit discipline, safety, attribution) bind whatever the user lane says; a user-lane statement that contradicts a project rule is reported, not obeyed. The exact precedence wording is part of the implementation.

memory.title: 4. User memory goes into the user project

p.USER-MEMORY-DEFAULT: By default, the facts an agent would otherwise write into a harness memory file (a local `MEMORY.md`, an auto-memory directory or similar) are written into the user project's `vibevm/vibespecs/` instead, as ordinary authored records that the user lane then loads.

p.USER-MEMORY-OPT-OUT: The default applies unless the user has explicitly decided otherwise and said so in a durable place (for example a setting in the user project or a statement in its user snippet). When opted out, agents use whatever memory mechanism the user chose and this law does not apply.

p.USER-MEMORY-CLASSIFICATION: The project-memory discipline still holds: a fact another contributor needs to build, review or understand a project belongs in that project's repository, never in the user project. Only facts about the user — preferences, working style, machine facts, cross-project conventions — go to the user project.

p.OVERRIDE-PURPOSE: Owner extension 2026-11-08. Everyone works with a project the same way, as recorded in git; a user who wants to work differently in that project keeps their own way in a per-user, per-project override project instead of committing it to the shared repository. The global user project is the outermost override for every project. The model is three layers: project ← project override ← global user project, the same ladder `.vibe/registry.local.toml` → `vibe.toml` → `~/.vibe/registry.toml` already uses for registries, generalised to the whole project.

p.OVERRIDE-SHAPE: An override project is an ordinary vibevm project like the user project (§2): own `vibe.toml`, lock, `vibedeps` and authored `vibevm/vibespecs`, its own compilation and its own boot lane. It never writes the project's tracked files or its lock, and a teammate's clone is unaffected by it.

p.OVERRIDE-LOCATION: Owner decision 2026-11-08: stored under the user's home, keyed by a project binding (repository identity plus checkout, the same binding the user-local steward contexts use), so it survives a re-clone and is shared by worktrees of one project. It is never stored inside the checkout. How a user enables, creates and selects an override is configurable; those mechanics and the exact binding key are settled at implementation.

p.OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE: Owner decision 2026-11-08: on conflict the more specific layer wins — project < global user project < project override. A per-project choice beats the user's general preference, as git's local beats global. Lanes load in the same order, project first, then the global user lane, then the project override lane, so the most specific text comes last. Non-overridable project rules still bind every layer (OVERRIDE-ADDITIVE).

p.OVERRIDE-ADDITIVE: Overrides add freely: extra packages, flows, skills, preferences. Taking away or replacing project rules is allowed only for what the project marks as overridable; commit discipline, attribution, safety and anything unmarked can only be supplemented. A layer statement contradicting a non-overridable project rule is reported, never obeyed (extends USER-LANE-PRECEDENCE).

p.OVERRIDE-SEPARATE-RESOLUTION: Each layer has its own lock and is resolved and compiled separately in this task; a package an override needs at a version different from the project's lives in the override's own tree. The override lane loads dynamically, like the user lane (USER-LANE-LAST), and never enters the project's own cache-stable prefix; the composed prefix of LAYERED-PREFIX is the one place where the layers join.

p.LAYERED-PREFIX: In scope of this task (owner decision 2026-11-08): one cache-stable boot prefix composed from project + global user project + project override, in the precedence order of OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE, with resolution across the layers. The project layer, as the most shared and most stable bytes, comes first, so the project's own prefix stays a byte-identical leading part of the composed one. Without a user project or override the composed prefix equals the project prefix. Until a user composes layers, the separately loaded lanes of §3 and OVERRIDE-SEPARATE-RESOLUTION remain the behaviour.

p.LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION: The composed prefix is personal and must never be committed. It is written inside the project's own `vibevm/` tree, next to the project's boot files, so an agent that looks around the file it was given finds the neighbouring files of the actual project and not of some other directory. The directory is ignored by a `.gitignore` that vibe writes into that directory itself (ignoring everything in it, including itself), never by editing the repository's root `.gitignore`. `vibe check` reports the composed prefix or its directory as an error when git tracks it. The exact path is settled at implementation (a sibling of `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/`, for example `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/local/`).

p.OVERRIDE-NO-AI-NATIVE-ANCHORS: Owner decision 2026-11-08: shared project code never anchors to a local layer. Checks written in the AI-native languages (`spec://` references, `specmark` scopes and `#[spec]`-style annotations, coverage and status checks) may target only the project's own specifications and its declared dependencies — never the global user project or a project override. Otherwise code committed for everyone would cite specifications that a teammate's checkout does not have. The AI-native checkers refuse such a reference with a message naming the reference, the local layer it points into and the fix; a layer's own specifications are never counted toward the project's coverage or status. This needs an update of the AI-native packages (`org.vibevm.ai-native.core-ai-native`, the Rust and TypeScript language packages and their MCP servers) as part of this task.

p.LAYERS-IN-TREE: Owner request 2026-11-08: `vibe tree` (plain, console TUI and vibeterm views, PROP-036) shows all three layers correctly — which layer each package, document and boot lane comes from, the effective result after precedence, and what a more specific layer supplements or replaces — and lets the user switch override layers on and off: hiding a layer in the view, and enabling or disabling a layer for the project itself (which then drops out of loading and of the composed prefix). The plain and JSON forms carry the same layer attribution.

p.USER-PROJECT-OPEN: The personal root, separation from MCP and explicit init/status lifecycle are settled in §2.1, with implementation still pending. Open: how an override is enabled, created and selected, and the exact project-binding key (§5); the composed-prefix path and how harnesses are pointed at it (LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION); how `-g` tells a specification package from an application package when a package is both; the exact hook by which a project boot index names the user lane (a generated dynamic entry with a `when` condition is the expected shape); how harnesses that read only one instructions file reach the user lane; the record layout and naming for agent-written memory facts; the opt-out setting; migration of an existing `MEMORY.md`; multi-machine sync (the user project is a git repository the user may push anywhere).
